items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: The other guy used to play with Eddie Pearson. He played with Paul Barber. He's a big, heavy set guy with a... He was a lot of sliding and stuff. Kind of a brassy, not really a real jazzy trombone player. Turbulon, I guess that was his name.

ctx.x: Do you think there's anything distinctive about the mechanics of New Orleans playing? How you hold your hands or how you finger?

Well, from my own observation, not particularly. I watch Percy's playing. He fingers his instrument extremely legitimate. Fingers all the way at the tips of his fingers. When he holds his horn and he's using his instrument, he does. But when he's playing and he's holding his horn with his left hand, he's not using the ring, you know. And the classical men don't like rings on horns. Because they say it interferes with the... When you play, see those two fingers go together like that. And that would interfere with…
What about half-valving though? That isn't legitimate. How some of them do that?
